decision: the 3-booted cap counts only ClaudioBot-UX-1..3; the already-booted iPhone 17 Pro (81E949D3) is the user's and is left alone
why: program forbids touching other devices; shutting it down could disrupt the user

decision: findings live in docs/ux-program/findings.tsv; ledger.tsv tracks steps
why: one file per concern keeps "next unfinished step" a one-line read

decision: scenario registry is TypeScript data (bin/scenarios.ts) and sessions.md is generated from it
why: one source for the setup, the rubric text and its mechanical check; a hand-written doc would drift from the checks

decision: a failed rubric item is a finding (exit 0); only a failed precondition fails the scenario (exit 2)
why: the audit wants findings recorded, and must never judge a situation it could not produce

decision: scenarios answer every permission card Allow once and record the tap
why: subagent and long Bash calls ask in default mode; a user would approve them, and auto mode would add a classifier as a second variable

decision: the phone leaves a thread (unwatch) before unread is judged and reopens it (watch after) to judge the thread
why: the bridge never marks a watched thread unread (catalog.ts), so a watcher that never leaves cannot see unread at all

decision: a lease's staleness is judged by its heartbeat only, not by pid liveness
why: lease acquire from the CLI exits right away, so another agent's lease has no live pid; the heartbeat is the one signal every holder keeps

decision: pairing stops at the app's confirmation; the Pair tap is left to an agent with the simulator tool, and no Debug auto-pair hook was added to the app
why: Step 0 changes no product code; an auto-confirm launch argument is a product call for the iOS owner

decision: S1 pins run_in_background false on its Agent calls and S1b pins true, each checked as a precondition
why: Claude Code's Agent tool defaults to async subagents and haiku chose either mode across runs; unpinned, S1 judged a different situation each time

decision: long foreground calls in scenarios use perl -e 'sleep N', not sleep N
why: Claude Code blocks a leading foreground sleep ("Blocked: standalone sleep 30"), so a sleep-based call never holds the turn

decision: in S8 the background command finishing is the judged outcome, not a precondition
why: the subagent started it (the situation was produced) and it never finished; reporting that as a failed precondition would hide the finding

decision: add a Debug-only launch argument that confirms a pairing link without the tap, for the simulator lane
why: simctl has no input; the simulator lane (S3, Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, dark mode, iPad checks) needs a paired app with no human; Debug-only keeps Release behavior unchanged

decision: reference study observes Claude Code desktop through its docs, on-disk session state and the CLI it wraps, not screen capture
why: computer-use needs a live user approval prompt, which would block an autonomous run

decision: simulator screenshots may show real session titles; they stay in the temp evidence folder, are never committed, and findings never quote real titles
why: the Sessions area must be audited on the real list (S7 mixes real and run sessions); keeping titles out of the repo and reports protects privacy without hiding the screen under audit

decision: X-ipad is judged by reading the app's size-class and split-view code plus iPhone landscape screenshots, and reported as a coverage gap
why: the program allows only the 3 iPhone pool devices; an iPad pool device would need the operator to allow cloning one

decision: ux-audit run caps at 6 rounds; when a run ends before two dry rounds, its survivors go into findings.tsv and the next run dedupes against them, continuing the loop
why: one run already took 3.3 h and 601 agents; findings per round fell 41,32,29,21,16,13 so the tail is real but shrinking

decision: Step 3 for Sessions starts on the 81 P0/P1 survivors while the next audit run continues in parallel; P2s are folded into a fix group only when it already touches their files, else they wait for the backlog
why: fixes land on main through worktrees and do not change the code the audit reads in this worktree; waiting hours for a dry run would idle the program

decision: an extra iPhone 17 Pro (D91C2F8B) was found booted during the audit; no auditor commanded it (transcripts checked), other Claude sessions on this Mac use it, so it is left alone
why: never touch devices outside the pool

decision: PR #3 (runner, pool, Debug auto-pair hook, docs) merged to main with a merge commit before fix groups start
why: fix worktrees branch off main and their verifiers need the runner; verified by the step 0 lease proof, bun test 2413 pass, iOS 277 pass

decision: severity merges suggested by the fix planner are not applied; skeptic severities stand
why: changing severities after the skeptic vote would bypass the verification it records; merges are handled by grouping

decision: G0: new protocol fields are absent-or-set, never null
why: absent and null are two spellings of one fact and Swift cannot round-trip both

decision: G0: tool-output fetch failures are an error frame with about.kind tool; session_tool_output.output stays non-null
why: nullable output would break older apps and allow output and error together

decision: G0: ErrorAbout and PushState are discriminated unions
why: a create error has no session; failing push always carries error and time

decision: G0: a stopped card reads as dismissed to protocol 2 apps and as closed in bot chat until G7 sets wording
why: expired would claim nobody answered in time

decision: G0: unserved partial stops and session_unqueue are refused with an error until G2/G3 serve them
why: silent ignore would lie about the stop

decision: G9: on background the app both unwatches threads and sends presence(false)
why: makes work finished while away mark the row unread with no bridge change, and marks seen when the user leaves

decision: G9: under 10 s away the app pings with a 2 s deadline, at 10 s or more it reconnects; first reply after connect has a 10 s deadline
why: fast return stays seamless, a dead socket is replaced quickly, a frozen Mac no longer hangs 60 s

decision: G9: retryNow() replaces retry() and reconnectNow()
why: one entry point; all callers migrated in the same PR

decision: G14 fix round (135d083) verified by root diff review instead of a fresh full verifier
why: the round was a 21-line change to exit-path reset and pgrep scoping, with the owner's SIGINT proof; a full swarm runs only for new behavior

decision: lease-proof rerun is deferred to a quiet pool; the G14 rerun showed its own five jobs never exceeded 3 booted and reclaim passed, but other agents held devices at the end
why: the proof asserts all pool devices shut down at the end, which only holds when no other agent leases

decision: after the session restarted on an OAuth expiry, each dead owner was replaced by a fresh owner working in the same worktree, and audit run 2 was resumed from its journal copied into the new session
why: the worktrees held the only copy of uncommitted work; fresh owners with consolidated briefs avoid trusting a dead agent's state

decision: G7: a stopped card reads "Stopped by you. It did not run."; a call allowed then cut short reads "Allowed once. Stopped by you before it finished."
why: protocol.ts closes a card as stopped only when the call never started, so "did not finish" would be false

decision: G7: folded approval cards stop growing at Dynamic Type AX2; the open card scales fully and VoiceOver still reads the command
why: three folded cards at AX5 push running work off screen, which is finding 077

decision: G7: "Show the step" tints the held step, not the whole work row
why: a work row can hold eight steps; tinting the row does not point at the call

decision: agents use the runner, xcrun simctl and demo launch args for simulator input, never the iOS Simulator MCP tool
why: that tool asks the user for device access, which blocks an unattended run

decision: G4: a subagent blocked on an approval card is never marked quiet; a background command is quiet only when the whole session is quiet
why: approval waits are on the user, not stuck; background commands send no progress, so their own start time would flag every long sleep

decision: G4: the failure cause gets its own line under the work-run header; live steps stay visible while the header is collapsed
why: a long cause wraps without pushing counts and clock off screen; every running agent stays labelled (F-SES-080)

decision: full finding evidence lives in /Users/tuba/Dev/projects/claudio-bot/.claude/ux-evidence/ (git-excluded in the main checkout), rebuilt from the audit journal after the temp folder was cleared
why: the macOS temp folder does not survive restarts; auditor text and evidence paths stay off GitHub

decision: program bookkeeping PRs (docs/ux-program only, no code) merge without a verifier
why: they change no behavior; each is a record of decisions already made

decision: simulator evidence from any --sim run that waited for a lease before the per-tree build fix is treated as unreliable; G9 is unaffected (its verifier confirmed the runner's build stamp matched the PR tree), audit run 2's simulator findings are rechecked by the Step 4 rerun on merged main
why: the shared ios-build folder let a waiting run install another worktree's app

decision: the app forces dark mode (ClaudioBotApp.swift:19), so dark-mode checks equal the default; light appearance is not a supported state today
why: recorded so auditors stop reporting identical dark/light shots as a gap

decision: G4: a run held only by approval shows an orange hand in its header, not a spinner
why: same glyph as a waiting step; a blocked run never looks busy (P-STATE-1)

decision: G1: Full output (session_tool) now masks secrets like the shown output; a repeat notification after a final one only adds a notice
why: Full output returned raw text even on main; releasing settled steps bounds the tail

decision: security-relevant fix rounds get a fresh verifier even when small
why: masking gaps are easy to miss in a diff read

decision: G7: when the user has scrolled up, thread size changes anchor to the top, and opening a folded card stops following the bottom
why: the bottom anchor pinned an expanding card above the screen at AX5; G5 and G11 inherit this in SessionThreadView

decision: G10: offline, row ages freeze at the last update and a working row shows a gray, still ring spoken as "working when last updated"; the Working chip hides its count
why: growing ages or spinning rings would imply the Mac is still reporting

decision: G10: the offline banner shows address, cause and Retry now / Edit address / Pair again from the first failed try, shortened at accessibility sizes; Retry is disabled while an attempt runs
why: the user can act at once and the buttons stay in reach at large text

decision: G1 merge gate for masking: no secret shape may reach the phone through a path G1 opened or changed; heuristic gaps that already reach the phone on main go to the backlog with a repro instead of blocking G1
why: masking is heuristic and can't be proven complete; G1 must not widen exposure, and older gaps get their own fix

decision: G1: maskProse masks a value-looking word after token/Basic/Bearer (has a digit, =, +, / or an inner capital), accepting rare over-masking such as "Bearer McGuire"
why: leaking a real credential is worse than hiding a rare proper noun

decision: G2: after a background task notifies, the session reads working (Stop offered) for up to 30 s until Claude Code's wake turn starts
why: hiding Stop for a turn about to run would be the same lie as the P0

decision: G2: the row's activity line reads "Waiting for approval: <tool>"; a subagent's card marks its task waiting while its Agent step keeps reading running
why: the subagent is alive; the card is what waits

decision: G2 gets a three-lane verifier swarm (rubric+protocol, simulator, code audit)
why: largest change of the program and the only P0; it also touches the runner's turn-end wait

decision: UI fixes that depend on a tap must be proven with a real tap (XCUITest host), not a probe build that triggers the action
why: G7's probe build hid a hang that only a real tap at AX4/AX5 showed

decision: G1: in descriptions, a 12+ character word after Bearer/Basic/token is masked, accepting over-masking like "Explain token «redacted»"; a description equal to its command is treated as the command
why: parity with main, which masked every label strictly; telling long words from tokens would need a word list

decision: runner PR #11 merged; simulator evidence from runs after this point records app.stamp and is trusted, earlier --sim evidence that waited for a lease is not
why: the stamp now hashes ios/ contents and install verifies the bundle

decision: G1: letters-only words under 12 characters after Bearer/Basic/token in a genuine description stay readable ("token for staging"), unlike main which masks them
why: readability of the model's own wording (finding 113); real tokens are longer or carry digits/symbols

decision: audit run 2 reached two dry rounds (rounds 4 and 5 added nothing) before the crash; its resume missed the cache and re-audited this worktree's pre-fix code while holding all 3 simulators, so it was stopped; its 91 unfiled candidates go through a dedupe-plus-skeptics workflow
why: the Step 2 dry criterion was already met; stale-code rounds compete with fix verifiers for simulators; Step 4 reruns the audit on merged main anyway

decision: G1 merged; a cut-short (…) task quote is masked strictly, accepting over-masking such as "Rotate the token «redacted» staging and…"
why: the cut can land inside a token; strict masking of truncated quotes can never show more than main

decision: G7: at accessibility text sizes a tapped folded approval card opens in a sheet; at default sizes it opens in place; thread scrolling stays as on main
why: at AX5 a card is taller than the screen, so in place it pushes its own header off; changing the thread scroll anchor caused a hang

decision: G2: a background command task is labelled by its masked command ("Background: sleep 60 && …"); a stopped notification announces a wake turn only when the bridge itself stopped the task
why: the row should say what is running; Claude Code wakes after a user stop but not after its own kill

decision: F-SES-170 filed as P0: at AX5 a swipe on a thread with running work freezes the app (main thread ~100% for minutes); fixed in its own group G16 ahead of G7's reveal re-test
why: the user cannot recover; it is already on main

decision: G7: a folded approval card opens in a sheet at every text size; the in-place path is dropped
why: in-place growth fights the thread's bottom anchor at default size too, hiding the header under the top bar

decision: G2: a background notification that lands during a running turn does not show a wake to the phone; one that lands after the turn ends shows working+Stop for up to 30 s until the wake turn; G3 posts the stop notice (reason stop) when Stop ends only background work
why: Claude Code folds a mid-turn notification into that turn but always wakes for one that lands after

decision: G3: a card whose Claude Code process died reads "closed", not "stopped"; any user stop during a run makes its outcome "stopped"; an early-stopped message reads "Stopped by you before Claude replied."
why: stop is the user's act and a crash is not; the bridge cannot tell whether Claude Code saved the message

decision: G3: "Stop and send" stops only the turn and leaves no cut; a duplicate failure notice is hidden when the transcript shows the same error within 2 minutes
why: background work keeps running; one failure, one line

decision: G3: a step still running once the session rests (no turn, no task, no other Claude Code busy) reads stopped "It ended without a result"; a failed turn keeps its prompt like a stopped one
why: no spinner may outlive the work; a failed turn can lose the message the same way a stopped one does

decision: G3: a step is ended at rest only when no other Claude Code has the session open (busy or idle); Claude Code's own "stopped by user" line is hidden only within 60 s of the bridge's stop notice for the same name
why: an idle terminal can still own running background work; a later same-named task must keep its line

decision: G16: the session thread is a plain VStack, not a LazyVStack, accepting ~30% more scroll CPU on 500-item threads
why: the lazy stack plus bottom anchor loops forever on rows taller than the screen at large text; a real thread opens one 120-item page

decision: G8: every thread item sorts by its time, ties by arrival, queued messages last; a lost or undecodable frame makes the app re-watch the thread for a snapshot
why: one rule on bridge, app and runner; no new protocol field

decision: G8: the user's bubble takes Claude Code's id and time when its copy lands, in place; F-SES-129's time change stays
why: keeping the send time would place a queued message inside the turn it waited behind

decision: G8: catalog flush (F-SES-044, F-SES-104) left unchanged
why: did not reproduce with 12 sessions on this Mac; recheck in Step 4

decision: G7: while "Show the step" marks a step (2 s tint), a change in thread height scrolls back to it
why: at large sizes the run lays out over several passes and the bottom anchor moves rows, so a single scroll lands on an old layout

decision: G12: the Sessions list orders needs you, then working by run start, then the rest by last activity; a row moves only when it changes group; positions hold while the list scrolls
why: a list that reorders with no status change is unreadable (S7.7); attention first

decision: G12: "Finished" shows on a row only while unread; failed, lost and stopped stay until the next send; the pending-mirror glyph is removed and a failed mirror reads "Not in Claude app"
why: every idle row would read Finished; a pending mirror asks nothing of the user

decision: G15: all four consequence lines show at every text size, capped at the first accessibility size; no Always button when the bridge offers no Always text; "Never" stays the visible word with a spoken hint saying what it does
why: a sighted AX5 user has no focus to follow; an Always that only allows once misleads

decision: G15: bot trust cards are recognised by the tool name "Claude Code settings" from gate.ts
why: no wire field yet; a real field would be better (backlog)

decision: a rubric item must be able to fail on a broken product; a judge that replays frames through its own copy of the app logic is a model check, not an acceptance item
why: G12's S7.7 rewrite passed 3000 of 3000 random histories

decision: app logs never carry command text in Release; diagnostic logs that quote user or tool content are DEBUG-only or .private
why: commands can hold credentials and the phone log is readable from a connected Mac

decision: G5: run clocks freeze only when no frame has arrived for 45 s or the app is offline, not when Claude Code's heardAt is old
why: a background sleep is silent while really running and the bridge still heartbeats every 25 s

decision: G5: a finished turn leaves the status line empty; failed, stopped and lost stay with "Send a message to start it again"; a status is spoken once it has held 500 ms; spoken cards are not repeated after reconnect
why: the reply above already says it finished; the turn end and its outcome arrive in separate frames

decision: G5: the thread waits 1.5 s after a run rests before speaking, so a late failed/stopped outcome is spoken instead of "finished"; the thread's Retry may restart a hung connect attempt
why: the bridge coalesces row updates for 500 ms; a hung connect should not lock Retry

decision: G5: a row arriving more than 1.5 s after rest may produce "Claude finished." then the real outcome
why: measured row lag is 319-619 ms; waiting longer would delay every finished announcement

decision: G6: a Stop that would also end background work always asks (Stop everything / Stop the turn only), even with no turn running; a turn alone stops at once
why: a background build is often why the session exists; asking costs one tap

decision: G6: a stop refusal clears once nothing runs; the thread keeps the bridge notice as the record
why: Claude Code can take a stop late, so a refusal can stop being true

decision: G6: Edit and resend / Edit on a queued message appends to the draft instead of replacing it
why: nothing the user typed is lost

decision: G6: composer chips stop growing at AX2 and the error line at AX3; spoken labels unchanged
why: uncapped, AX5 pushed the text field off screen

decision: G6: at accessibility sizes the composer field shows 2 lines and scrolls; the error line under the composer stops growing at AX1 and the status line at AX3
why: so a long draft never draws over chips or the refusal

decision: G6: with the keyboard up at accessibility sizes the status line keeps one line with an ellipsis, chips show icons only (queued chip keeps its count), Dismiss becomes a glyph and the bar gets a solid background; full words return when the keyboard hides; spoken labels unchanged
why: the bar must fit above the keyboard at AX3-AX5 without drawing text outside its frame

decision: G6: a refused stop belongs to the turn it targeted; after a newer turn starts the slot is a plain Stop with the background-work confirmation
why: Stop again must never widen to work the user did not ask to stop

decision: G17: new bridge-only group for stop/restart honesty (F-SES-173, F-SES-174 and stop-notice backlog items), run now in parallel with G6 and before G13 on own.ts
why: it touches no iOS files, so it can use the time G6 is still in review; G13 then rebases on it
